lessons.title: Obstetric Emergencies: PPH, eclampsia & cardiac arrest in pregnancy
lessons.summary: OB emergencies combine hemorrhage, airway difficulty, altered physiology and two-patient considerations. PPH and cardiac arrest are strongly time-sensitive.

sections.title: 1) Postpartum hemorrhage
paragraphs: PPH may occur without obvious risk factors. Quantify blood loss when possible, assess vitals/perfusion, uterine tone and source of bleeding. The 2025 WHO consolidated guideline emphasizes earlier recognition and rapid bundle-based treatment.

sections.title: 2) WHO 2025 MOTIVE bundle
paragraphs: Once PPH is diagnosed, WHO highlights immediate coordinated actions: uterine Massage, Oxytocic drugs, Tranexamic acid, IV fluids, Vaginal/genital tract examination, and Escalation of care.

sections.title: 3) TXA timing
paragraphs: WHO evidence supports early IV TXA for PPH as part of treatment; benefit decreases with delay and administration beyond 3 h after birth is not supported by the cited evidence. Local EMS scope/protocol determines prehospital use.

sections.title: 4) Pregnancy cardiac arrest
paragraphs: AHA 2025: standard high-quality CPR + continuous left lateral uterine displacement when fundus at/above umbilicus; prepare resuscitative delivery immediately with goal completion by 5 min if no ROSC, depending on resources.

sections.title: 5) Eclampsia
paragraphs: Pregnancy/postpartum seizure with hypertension features requires airway/oxygenation protection, magnesium-based treatment per obstetric protocol, BP management and rapid obstetric destination.

key_points: PPH requires early recognition and coordinated response
Pregnancy arrest: left uterine displacement + prepare delivery
Airway may be more difficult in pregnancy
quick_review: Goal resuscitative delivery by 5 min if no ROSC

research_updates.title: WHO consolidated PPH guideline
research_updates.takeaway: WHO/FIGO/ICM consolidated 51 evidence-based recommendations and emphasized earlier diagnosis and immediate MOTIVE bundle treatment.

quiz.q: WHO 2025 PPH bundle acronym includes TXA?
quiz.explain: Tranexamic acid is part of the MOTIVE bundle.

quiz.q: AHA pregnancy arrest target for resuscitative delivery if no ROSC?
quiz.explain: AHA 2025 recommends preparing immediately with a goal to complete by 5 minutes when indicated/resources allow.

lessons.title: Normal Prehospital Delivery & Immediate Newborn Care
lessons.summary: เตรียม mother + newborn simultaneously: recognize imminent birth, support physiologic delivery and prevent hypothermia.

sections.title: 1) Is birth imminent?
paragraphs: Strong regular contractions, urge to push, crowning, multiparity and prior rapid delivery increase likelihood. Check gestation, membranes, bleeding, complications and number of fetuses if known.

sections.title: 2) Support delivery
paragraphs: Provide privacy, clean environment and controlled support; do not pull the baby. Check for nuchal cord according to training and manage shoulder dystocia if encountered.

sections.title: 3) After birth
paragraphs: Assess breathing/tone, provide warmth/skin-to-skin when appropriate, manage cord according to current neonatal plan, and observe maternal bleeding/uterine tone.

sections.title: 4) Placenta
paragraphs: Do not apply uncontrolled traction. Preserve placenta/tissue for hospital assessment and monitor for PPH.

lessons.title: Preeclampsia & Eclampsia: Seizure in Pregnancy/Postpartum
lessons.summary: eclampsia can occur antepartum, intrapartum or postpartum and requires simultaneous seizure, BP and obstetric management.

sections.title: 1) Preeclampsia spectrum
paragraphs: Hypertension after mid-pregnancy with organ dysfunction can involve brain, liver, kidney, platelets and placenta. Severe headache, visual symptoms, RUQ/epigastric pain and pulmonary edema are danger signs.

sections.title: 2) Eclampsia
paragraphs: Generalized seizure in a patient with preeclampsia spectrum after excluding other causes. Protect airway, prevent injury and support oxygenation.

sections.title: 3) Magnesium sulfate
paragraphs: Magnesium is the key anticonvulsant for eclampsia prevention/treatment in obstetric protocols; exact dose/route must follow local guideline. Monitor respiratory depression and reflexes when relevant.

sections.title: 4) Severe hypertension
paragraphs: Persistent severe BP requires urgent obstetric antihypertensive management because of stroke risk; transport to obstetric-capable facility.

lessons.title: Ectopic Pregnancy & Early-Pregnancy Hemorrhagic Shock
lessons.summary: reproductive-age patient + abdominal pain/syncope/shock = consider ectopic even without known pregnancy.

sections.title: 1) Pathophysiology
paragraphs: Implantation outside uterine cavity, most often tubal, can rupture and cause life-threatening intra-abdominal bleeding.

sections.title: 2) Presentation
paragraphs: Unilateral/lower abdominal pain, vaginal bleeding, shoulder-tip pain, syncope or shock. Symptoms may be nonspecific and vaginal bleeding can be minimal despite major hemoperitoneum.

sections.title: 3) Risk factors
paragraphs: Prior ectopic, tubal surgery/disease, assisted reproduction and IUD pregnancy increase risk, but many patients lack classic risk factors.

sections.title: 4) EMS priorities
paragraphs: Treat shock, avoid delays, obtain pregnancy/gestational history and alert an appropriate receiving facility. Definitive care is surgical/gynecologic evaluation.

lessons.title: Shoulder Dystocia: Time-Critical Delivery Maneuvers
lessons.summary: หลังศีรษะคลอดแล้วไหล่ติดเป็น obstetric emergency—recognize and perform trained maneuvers promptly.

sections.title: 1) Recognition
paragraphs: Head delivers but retracts against perineum (“turtle sign”) or shoulders fail to deliver with normal gentle traction.

sections.title: 2) First maneuvers
paragraphs: Call for help, note time, avoid fundal pressure. McRoberts positioning and suprapubic pressure are common first-line maneuvers; subsequent maneuvers depend on training/protocol.

sections.title: 3) Avoid harmful actions
paragraphs: Do not apply excessive traction to fetal head/neck and do not use fundal pressure.

sections.title: 4) After delivery
paragraphs: Prepare neonatal resuscitation and assess maternal bleeding/trauma. Document sequence and timing.

lessons.title: Cardiac Arrest in Pregnancy: Maternal Resuscitation & Resuscitative Delivery
lessons.summary: resuscitate the mother aggressively while accounting for aortocaval compression and pregnancy-specific reversible causes.

sections.title: 1) CPR modifications
paragraphs: High-quality CPR and standard defibrillation remain critical. In later pregnancy, manual left uterine displacement can reduce aortocaval compression while keeping the patient supine for effective compressions.

sections.title: 2) Airway
paragraphs: Pregnancy increases aspiration risk and airway difficulty; prepare experienced airway support early without delaying compressions/defibrillation.

sections.title: 3) Causes
paragraphs: Hemorrhage, PE, eclampsia, amniotic fluid embolism, sepsis, cardiac disease and anesthesia/toxicity are important pregnancy-specific contexts alongside usual Hs & Ts.

sections.title: 4) Resuscitative delivery
paragraphs: When indicated in a sufficiently advanced pregnancy and ROSC does not occur promptly, resuscitative delivery can improve maternal resuscitation by relieving aortocaval compression and may benefit fetus; timing/system protocol and trained team are essential.
